post.title: 86 free apps built out of pure spite · October 2026
post.caption: October's best free apps from people who read a pricing page and built the thing themselves: what each one replaces, what that costs, and who refused a one-time $4.99.

say: I'm not paying for Whisper Flow

segments.title: here we go
turns: <title><sfx whoosh>This is Spiteware Monthly. Welcome, everybody. I hope nothing renewed while you were asleep. I'm Vera.
<stats>Somebody gets annoyed at a price, builds the thing, and gives it away. We listed {LIVE} of those in October. Here are the best ones, and the bills they're answering.
<eq>You're about to ask if I cancelled anything.
Eleven subscriptions, and a meditation app you swore you'd try once more.
<fx 🫁 boing>I tried it. I'll report at the end.

segments.title: it's already yours
turns: <gap 0.6>Okay. First pattern. It's yours, and there's a toll on it.
<gap 0.3><bill velocity>Flightradar24 now charges for anything older than twelve hours. <app velocity>Andrew built Velocity. It records every plane and ship to your own disk.
<fx ✈️ pop>So yesterday is a premium feature.
<gap 0.3><bill cairn-notes>Obsidian charges $5 a month to move your own Markdown between your own devices. <app cairn-notes>Lucas Pospor built Cairn Notes.
<bill tern>Termius Pro. $10 a month to sync your server list. <app tern>Moonn built tern. It syncs to a Git repo you own.
<fx 💬 pop tl>Anybody out there paying for sync? Tell us.
<gap 0.3><bill collectarr>CLZ wants a separate subscription per shelf. <app collectarr>SaiTatter built Collectarr.

segments.title: on somebody's server
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Next pattern. Your own voice, on somebody else's server.
<gap 0.3><bill parrot>Otter Pro is $16.99 a month, and your calls go to its servers. <app parrot>Uygar Turantekin built Parrot. It transcribes on your own Mac, with no bot in the meeting.
<fx 🦜 pop>I always wave at the bot.
<bill sada>Word's Transcribe needs a Microsoft 365 subscription and stops at 300 minutes a month. <app sada>Mohammed Khaled Mahmoud built sada. It runs on your own PC, inside Word.

segments.title: wall of shame
turns: <gap 0.7><bill mylittlesoundpad><sfx drumroll>Okay. Wall of shame. Four products tied this month at two replacements each, so I picked. Soundpad. It plays sound files. $4.99.
<wall>Two of them. MyLittleSoundpad, <wall all>and Onion Board. One builder's reason: not wanting to pay three dollars.
<fx 💬 pop br>Would you build an app to save three dollars? I'd like to meet you.

segments.title: by the seat
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Seats. I sold them for six years. Now I buy them. I own a bike shop. <fx 🪑 pop>Seven people, seven seats, on everything.
<gap 0.3>Then sit down. <bill stepcast>Arcade Growth is $50 a seat, a month, to replay your own clicks. <app stepcast>Arda built Stepcast.
$350 a month. I did it before you sat down.
<gap 0.3><bill lindowin>Docker Desktop wants $24 a seat once a company passes 250 people. <app lindowin>Alejandro Lozano built lindowin. Same commands, no invoice.

segments.title: one little thing
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Okay. A whole plan, for one little thing.
<gap 0.3><bill wordpaste>TinyMCE puts clean Word paste in its $145 a month plan. <app wordpaste>MD Rifat Hossain built wordpaste.
<gap 0.3><bill cadenzato>Noisli turns the rain off after 90 minutes unless you pay $12 a month. <app cadenzato>Cadenzato synthesizes it forever.
<fx 🌧️ pop>I ride in that on Saturdays. Nobody's billed me yet.
<gap 0.3><bill glossyshots>CleanShot wants $10 a month to make one presentable. <app glossyshots>abg5f built Glossyshots, for Windows.
<gap 0.3><bill baldente>AlDente charges €11.49 a year to stop your Mac at 80%. <app baldente>close design built BalDente.
<eq>My brother Sami says he could build all of those in a weekend.
<fx 🚧 squeak>He has a lot of weekends.

segments.title: on the site
turns: <gap 0.7><site rules>Quick site tip. There's a rules page. Nobody pays to be on the list.
I asked what a boosted spot would cost.
There's a whole page saying you can't.
<fx 🚪 buzzer>I read it. Two gates, a score out of ten, and no door for a salesman.

segments.title: the bigger bills
turns: <gap 0.3><bill ketchup>SketchUp Pro is $33.25 a month to push a rectangle into a box. <app ketchup>Dan Coulombe built KetchUp.
<fx 🍅 pop>KetchUp. I have nothing to add.
<gap 0.3><bill hedwig>Instantly wants $97 a month to send cold email from inboxes you already own. <app hedwig>Gabriel Cebria Oliveira built Hedwig.
<fx 💬 pop>I have sent that email. Is anybody watching paying for this right now?

segments.title: say it in the name
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Last two. Neither one hid how it felt.
<gap 0.3><bill lensprout>Screen Studio is $29 a month. <app lensprout>Muchamad Yuda Tri Ananda built Lensprout. Its pricing table is all zeros.
<bill local-dictation>Then here's a $15 a month dictation bill. <app local-dictation>Yosef Shammout built Local Dictation. The name of the repo: imnotpayingforwisprflow.

segments.title: spite of the month
turns: <fx 🕯️ gong>It said welcome back, and it asked me to breathe.
I went to cancel. It offered me the annual plan.
<fx 🤦 buzzer>I took it. I was very calm when I clicked.
Still eleven, then. Your pick. Spite of the month.
<spite local-dictation><sfx fanfare>Local Dictation. Other people write a blog post. This one just named the repo.
<eq>Software should still cost money. It can stop telling me to breathe.
<outro>Everything we mentioned is linked below, and there are {MORE} more from October at spiteware.ai.
Which one would you cancel something for? Tell us. Got a grudge with a download link? Send it in.
<outro sub><fx 🔔 ding br>Subscribe and hit the bell, and the November grudges will find you.
See you in December. Cancel something.
